purpose: A repeatable test battery that finds each car's USABLE WINDOW on every tuning slider — so a from-scratch tune can be fitted to a specific course archetype or PI class with evidence instead of guesswork. A 'reasonable limit' here means: the slider range inside which the car still passes the relevant test; outside it, a named symptom appears.
confidence: method — the battery is designed from verified instruments + the project's slider-pole data, but the battery AS A WHOLE is untested. Each test promotes to player-verified as Jett runs it and reports.

lab_conditions.rivals_is_the_lab: Rivals events run FIXED weather and time of day — the only repeatable test environment in the game. Free-roam has weather drift; never compare runs across different free-roam sessions.
lab_conditions.one_variable: Change ONE slider between iterations. Two changes that both 'feel faster' can be one gain hiding one loss.
lab_conditions.noise_control: Driver variance is the biggest error source. Use 3-lap MEDIANS (not best laps), judge via ghost SECTOR deltas rather than whole-lap feel, and freeze your assist config across every test (board meta: ABS on, TCS off, STM off).
lab_conditions.bisection: To find a limit: start at the baseline value, jump the slider to its extreme. If the test FAILS, move halfway back toward baseline; repeat until it passes. The last failing and first passing values bracket the limit. ~4 iterations brackets any slider to useful precision.
lab_conditions.record_everything: Every found limit goes in results_log with the car, surface, and the symptom at the limit. A window without its symptom is half a data point.

instrumentation.what: Tune-screen Performance panel: lateral G @60/@120 mph, 0-60, 0-100, top speed, braking 60-0 ft and 100-0 ft, mechanical balance, aero balance, aero efficiency.
instrumentation.use: INSTANT static bisection with zero driving. If a readout responds to a slider, you can find that slider's knee-point in a minute from the menu.

instrumentation.what: Driving telemetry overlay: per-tire temps (inner/middle/outer), live/hot PSI, suspension travel.
instrumentation.status: needs_ingame — FH5 had it (hold the extras button); FH6 keybind and data set UNVERIFIED. First telemetry test should start by confirming the overlay exists and what it shows.
instrumentation.use: Ground truth for camber (temp spread), cold-vs-hot pressure, and bottoming-out.

instrumentation.what: Own-ghost sector deltas + 3-lap median lap times on a fixed Rivals event.
instrumentation.use: The only truth that matters at the end. Every accepted change must survive the lap supertest.

instrumentation.what: Drag-strip Rivals times (fixed distance, fixed surface).
instrumentation.use: Launch/gearing scoring with no cornering noise.

test_zero.name: Sensitivity matrix — run this ONCE before everything
test_zero.procedure: On a settled build, move each slider from min to max while watching the Performance panel. Record WHICH readouts move and roughly how much. Some readouts may respond only to PARTS, not sliders — knowing which sliders are panel-visible vs drive-to-measure decides which battery track (static vs dynamic) each slider uses.
test_zero.output: A slider × readout sensitivity map. This is the highest-value 20 minutes in the whole battery: it converts unknown sliders into free static tests.
findings: PLAYER-VERIFIED (Supra range sweep screenshots): the Performance panel LIVE-RESIMULATES on slider change — 'SIMULATING...' states observed mid-change, and 'FAILED!' states at extreme configs (the sim cannot complete e.g. braking runs at 0% pressure, top-speed runs at extreme gearing). The panel is a working instrument; FAILED at an extreme is itself a data point (the config is undrivable). Full per-readout sensitivity map still pending — several captures show large readout swings (0-60 3.06s vs 5.9s) that are CONFOUNDED across multiple changed sliders; do single-slider sweeps to attribute.

static_tests.name: Aero balance window
static_tests.procedure: Hold total downforce roughly constant, shift F/R split, watch the balance readout. Then find min-total and max-total downforce that keep balance in the window.
static_tests.pass: Balance 0.42-0.50 (slightly forward of mechanical balance for stability; project data: 0.40-0.50 target band, 0.52 observed on the Golf).
static_tests.fail_symptom: Below window = high-speed push (front washes); above = high-speed loose (rear light).
static_tests.confidence: probable — band from gamingpromax + observed build; verify the band per car class

static_tests.name: Braking distance floor
static_tests.procedure: Bisect pressure upward until the panel distance stops improving — that's the panel's knee. The true limit (lockup) is found in the dynamic braking test; the panel knee is your starting point.
static_tests.pass: Panel distance within a few ft of the best value found
static_tests.fail_symptom: Distances worsen past the knee (modeled lockup)

static_tests.name: Gearing envelope (final drive)
static_tests.procedure: Bisect FD between 'too long' (0-60 degrades, top speed unreachable on course) and 'too short' (top speed below the course's Vmax need). Course Vmax needs come from course_fitting archetypes.
static_tests.pass: Top speed ≥ course Vmax need AND 0-60 within 0.2s of the best achievable at that constraint
static_tests.fail_symptom: Redline mid-straight (too short) or dead acceleration out of slow corners (too long)

dynamic_tests.name: Hot tire pressure
dynamic_tests.venue: Any Rivals circuit, 3 minutes at race pace
dynamic_tests.measure: Hot PSI via telemetry (needs_ingame); fallback: lateral-G validation lap + slide feel
dynamic_tests.pass: Hot pressure 31-33 PSI both axles (project band: cold 27-28 road / ~3 lower dirt)
dynamic_tests.fail_symptom: Over: skittish, small contact patch, snap breakaway. Under: mushy turn-in, slow response, overheating shoulders.
dynamic_tests.limit_finding: Cold-PSI window per axle = the range that lands hot pressure in band after 3 minutes
dynamic_tests.confidence: probable — 31-33 band is community consensus, verify per compound

dynamic_tests.name: Camber by temperature spread
dynamic_tests.venue: Longest steady corner on the test course (or a roundabout at steady speed)
dynamic_tests.measure: Inner/middle/outer tire temps immediately after the corner (telemetry, needs_ingame)
dynamic_tests.pass: Inner edge 10-15°F hotter than outer, middle in between
dynamic_tests.fail_symptom: Outer hottest = not enough negative camber (add). Inner scorched + middle cold = too much (reduce).
dynamic_tests.limit_finding: No-telemetry fallback: bisect camber on ghost sector delta through the longest corner — the delta knee IS the limit
dynamic_tests.confidence: method — classic race doctrine, FH6 telemetry unverified

dynamic_tests.name: Braking stability & true lockup
dynamic_tests.venue: Drag strip or straight with a fixed brake marker
dynamic_tests.measure: Stopping point vs marker; visual lockup; car rotation under braking
dynamic_tests.pass: Straight stop, no lock flare, real distance within ~5% of panel figure
dynamic_tests.fail_symptom: Pressure too high: fronts lock (straight slide). Balance too far back: rear walks sideways under braking — the scarier failure.
dynamic_tests.limit_finding: Raise pressure until first lockup, back off one notch = pressure ceiling. Then move balance rearward until the tail stirs, back off 2% = balance floor.

dynamic_tests.name: Corner-entry rotation (understeer gate)
dynamic_tests.venue: Benchmark hairpin (pick ONE per course and reuse it)
dynamic_tests.measure: Ghost sector delta through the hairpin + apex-hit subjective
dynamic_tests.pass: Apex reachable at target entry speed without early-apex push; sector delta neutral or better
dynamic_tests.fail_symptom: Push past apex = still understeering (keep going). Nose darts / rear nervous on entry = overshot (back off last change).
dynamic_tests.limit_finding: One slider at a time in the listed order; the order IS the doctrine (cheapest fix first)
dynamic_tests.confidence: probable — slider poles verified from tune-screen recording; order is doctrine

dynamic_tests.name: Corner-exit traction (oversteer gate)
dynamic_tests.venue: Same benchmark hairpin, focus on throttle-on phase
dynamic_tests.measure: Earliest full-throttle point vs ghost; correction count
dynamic_tests.pass: Full throttle one car-length past apex with zero countersteer
dynamic_tests.fail_symptom: Wheelspin/slide on exit = too much diff lock or rear too stiff
dynamic_tests.limit_finding: Diff accel ceiling = highest value with a clean full-throttle exit; that ceiling differs road (~40-60%) vs dirt (higher for predictability)

dynamic_tests.name: Kerb & bump compliance
dynamic_tests.venue: Curb-heavy chicane or the course's roughest section
dynamic_tests.measure: Car settles within ~1 oscillation after the kerb; line held; no bottoming (sparks/thud)
dynamic_tests.pass: Can attack the kerb repeatedly with a consistent line
dynamic_tests.fail_symptom: Skip/hop off kerbs = too stiff (springs/bump). Wallowing after = too soft on rebound. Sparks/scrape = ride height below the course floor.
dynamic_tests.limit_finding: Springs: bisect down from calculator value until wallow appears, up until skip appears — that's THE window. Ride height floor: lower one notch at a time on the worst compression until first scrape, then +1 notch = course floor.

dynamic_tests.name: High-speed stability
dynamic_tests.venue: Fastest sweeper/straight on course, flat out
dynamic_tests.measure: Steering-correction count at Vmax; snap events
dynamic_tests.pass: Hands-steady at Vmax through the sweeper
dynamic_tests.fail_symptom: Wandering = rear toe 0 with loose rear; snap on lift = rebound/aero rear insufficient
dynamic_tests.limit_finding: Rear toe-in is nearly free stability but costs a hair of rotation — find the minimum that passes

dynamic_tests.name: The lap supertest (every accepted change re-earns its place)
dynamic_tests.measure: 3-lap median vs stored ghost; sector deltas
dynamic_tests.pass: Median improves, OR target sector improves without losing more elsewhere
dynamic_tests.fail_symptom: A change that 'feels better' but tests slower — revert it. Feel lies; medians don't.
dynamic_tests.limit_finding: This is the arbiter for every window the other tests propose
dynamic_tests.confidence: verified — this is just measurement discipline

symptom_matrix.symptom: Oversteer on entry (rear steps in on brake/lift)
symptom_matrix.tertiary: diff decel UP (corrected 2026-08-10 — in-game Description, primary: raising rear Decel 'can reduce lift off oversteer'; the old 'down' entry fed a live coaching error)

symptom_matrix.symptom: Floaty after crests, slow to settle
Kerbs throw the car off line

course_fitting.note: Which tests DOMINATE per course archetype (archetypes from the Rivals track data). Run the dominant tests on that course's own benchmark corners — a window found on the wrong course is the wrong window.

archetypes.gearing: short-mid FD, 2nd-4th gear spacing matters most
short FD, tall 1st for loose-surface launch

class_fitting.note: PI class decides WHERE in each window you sit. The battery finds the window; the class picks the point.
rules: D-B: PI is scarce and grip is king — sit at the grip edge of every window (max compliance, modest power). Panel braking/lateral-G per PI point spent is the best value metric.
A-S1: balanced — windows are widest here; the lap supertest arbitrates.
S2-R: stability tests gain weight (high-speed-stability, aero-window) because speeds make instability terminal; expect to give up rotation for stability.

results_log.instructions: One row per found limit. The window is the deliverable; the symptom at the limit is the evidence. Report rows in-session and they get added here — this log is what makes the next tune START from knowledge.

example_row.symptom_at_limit: front lockup into the hairpin at 120%

cornering_envelope.concept: The car's max-holdable corner is a CURVE, not a number: radius = v^2 / (g x latG), and latG itself = mechanical grip (constant) + aero grip (grows with v^2). The Performance panel's TWO lateral-G readouts (@60 and @120 mph) pin both components exactly - so the whole envelope is measurable from the tune menu, per build, in seconds.
cornering_envelope.model: latG(v) = a + b*v^2 fitted through the two panel points; max corner speed for radius r solves v^2 = g*r*latG(v) -> v = sqrt(g*r*a / (1 - g*r*b)). Units: ft, ft/s, g=32.17.

lift_whole_curve_mechanical: ARB & spring BALANCE (the first axle to give up sets the radius - balancing reclaims wasted grip)
bend_fast_end_aero: front/rear downforce - invisible in slow hairpins, dominant in fast sweepers
ceiling_build_not_sliders: tire compound tier and weight set the ceiling; sliders approach it (escalation rule)

cornering_envelope.workflow: Read latG@60 and latG@120 off the Performance panel -> enter in the widget -> the envelope draws. After any phase-3 slider change, re-read the panel: mech sliders move the @60 number, aero moves the spread between the two. This is the static half of the camber/pressure tests - the panel IS the instrument.
cornering_envelope.defaults_note: Widget defaults to the verified Golf R observed build (1.11 @60 / 1.13 @120, player screenshot 2026-06-08) so it renders real data before you enter your own.
cornering_envelope.confidence: model = standard vehicle dynamics; panel readouts = verified instrument; the a+b*v^2 fit assumes the panel's two points are steady-state limits, which matches their in-game description

capture_protocol.purpose: Minimum screenshots for a session partner (or future you) to fully reconstruct a build. The tune screen shows the Performance panel on every tab, so each tab shot carries the derived stats for free.
core_3: 1. TIRES TAB — header (car, PI/class) + pressures + the full Performance panel (lateral G @60/@120 = envelope inputs, 0-60, top speed, braking, balances). Half the build in one shot.
2. GEARING TAB — final drive, all ratios, gear count (reveals transmission), speed graph.
3. SPRINGS TAB with a slider SELECTED — rates + ride heights + the slider MIN-MAX range (the calculator input a casual shot misses).
capture_protocol.plus_text: One sentence of parts provenance instead of upgrade-menu shots: swap? compound? aero kit? gearbox tier? Locked tune tabs also reveal missing parts via their banners - mention them.
capture_protocol.full_record: Core 3 + alignment + damping + diff tabs = 6 shots (AWD) / 5 (RWD) captures every number. ARB/aero/brakes only if unlocked and non-default.
capture_protocol.handling_problem: Often ONE shot: the tab that owns the problem PHASE (per the phase map) - the Performance panel rides along free.
capture_protocol.confidence: protocol built on the verified tune-screen layout (Golf R recording 2026-06-08); panel-on-every-tab assumption verified in that footage

build_forensics.problem: FH6 downloaded tunes are LOCKED (player-verified): no parts list, no slider values. But the game leaks the build through observable surfaces — a locked tune is a black box with gauges on the outside. This protocol reconstructs the parts list so the build can be replicated on a second copy of the car WITH unlocked sliders.

instruments.when: BEFORE downloading — works on ANY tune in the browser
instruments.what: The tune detail pane is the game's own stock-vs-tuned diff: Previous (stock) vs New (tuned) across 13+ Car Stat rows, INCLUDING three outright parts rows — Suspension tier, Tire Compound, Drivetrain. Plus replication targets: power, torque, weight, top speed, 0-60, lateral G, PWR, aero efficiency, aero balance, mechanical balance; the radar bars; base PI -> final PI; and the share code via [P] View Share Code. LIVE DIFF (player-verified 2026-08-10): the Previous column tracks the car's CURRENT setup, not frozen stock — after installing a part, reopening the tune page shows the updated value. Replication is complete when every Previous equals its New.
instruments.status: player-verified 2026-08-10 (Viper GTS ACR '99 tune-browser screenshots). The Car Stat column SCROLLS — check for rows below Drivetrain (brakes/aero tiers may be listed). PLAYER-VERIFIED 2026-08-10: this pane exists ONLY in the Tunes browser — the upgrade shop does NOT show the full Car Stat table while buying parts (per-part deltas only).

instruments.when: AFTER download — for locked builds already in the garage
instruments.what: My Cars card + two stat pages (L Toggle Stats): bars (Speed/Handling/Accel/Launch/Braking/Offroad), tire-compound and drivetrain badges on the card, value CR, then power, torque, weight, front %, and DISPLACEMENT — which exposes big-bore engine upgrades (a stock 8.4L reading 9.00L = displacement tier installed).

Engine audio settles aspiration in one corner (turbo whistle/blow-off vs NA howl); HUD gear count reveals transmission tier (6 = stock-ish, 7-10 = race); RPM at a fixed speed in a fixed gear reads effective gearing straight through the lock; rev limit hints race internals; photo mode side-by-side vs a stock copy shows aero kit and ride height.
instruments.status: method — each channel individually sound; protocol untested as a battery

instruments.when: Final step — rebuild the parts list on a second copy
instruments.what: Solve constraints in this order: (1) install the directly-read parts (drivetrain swap, compound, suspension tier); (2) match displacement; (3) match hp AND torque SIMULTANEOUSLY — the pair collapses aspiration+parts fast because turbos overshoot torque at a given hp; (4) match weight (fixed reduction tiers; remember swaps ADD weight before reduction subtracts); (5) cross-check front % / mechanical balance; (6) PI must land EXACTLY on the tune's number; (7) stat bars are the final checksum. The replica is a functionally identical chassis with UNLOCKED sliders — fit your own tune, using the locked copy's gearing forensics as the starting point. COMPLETION CRITERION (player-verified): reopen the tune's browser page between shop visits — the live Previous column ticks off each matched row; all-rows-matched + PI exact = certified replica.

catalog_quirks.finding: PLAYER-VERIFIED: the Viper GTS ACR '99 Springs and Dampers catalog offers only Stock / Drift / Rally — NO Race tier. Part catalogs are CAR-SPECIFIC; never assume the full Street/Sport/Race/Rally/Drift/Offroad ladder exists on a given car.
catalog_quirks.substitution_rule: All adjustable spring tiers unlock the SAME slider set (springs, ride height, gates damper tuning) — they differ only in default values and PI cost (guides describe rally springs as race values halved). For a road/circuit replica on a car lacking Race springs: use DRIFT springs (stiff/low road-biased defaults) over Rally (soft/tall dirt defaults), then set your own values.
catalog_quirks.pane_label_hypothesis: RESOLVED, PLAYER-VERIFIED 2026-08-10: the 'Suspension' row is a coarse ADJUSTABILITY bucket — after installing DRIFT springs on the Viper GTS ACR '99, the Previous column read 'Race'. Twin confirmation: 'Previous' tracks the car's CURRENT setup (it updated after the install), making the pane a live replica-vs-target diff. Corollary: the case study's stock baselines are valid — the original capture's Previous column (B 598 / Sport / Standard / RWD) shows the car was stock at capture time.
catalog_quirks.pi_checksum_as_arbiter: Drift vs Rally springs cost different PI. With the rest of the build matched, whichever choice lands total PI EXACTLY on the tune's number (here S1 800) is the tuner's actual part — evidence, not guesswork.
catalog_quirks.confidence: catalog gap player-verified; same-sliders rule FH5-inherited + guide-consistent (probable); pane hypothesis untested
catalog_quirks.suspension_row_addendum: 4C confirms the row reads real installed tiers: player's actual Race springs displayed 'Race' (vs Viper GTS ACR case where DRIFT springs displayed 'Race' — adjustable tiers bucket to 'Race', but Street/Sport display as themselves). Catalogs remain per-car: the 4C offers true Race springs, the Viper does not.

build_forensics.doctrine: PLAYER-STATED 2026-08-10: the protocol's deliverable is the DISCRETE PARTS MANIFEST, not slider values. Sliders are ephemeral — Jett re-fits them to their own driving regardless. Parts are where the tuner's intelligence lives: how the PI budget was allocated across drivetrain/engine/weight/grip is the unrecoverable-by-guessing knowledge. Every decoded build gets recorded as a manifest with per-part evidence tiers (verified = pane row or direct observation; probable = delta inference; open = PI-checksum residual).

build_forensics.value_check_refuted: PLAYER-VERIFIED 2026-08-10: My Cars card value IGNORES installed parts — stock 4C (A 644) and fully built 4C (S1 800, AWD swap + engine swap) both show 69,350 CR. The 'value delta = parts spend' bound proposed in the Viper case is REFUTED; remove it from the instrument list.
build_forensics.suspension_row_note: The compare pane's Suspension row tracks real tiers (Street/Sport/Race-bucket). Case study 2 shows Street->Street: top-rank tuners sometimes SKIP adjustable suspension to spend PI on power — do not assume race suspension is always present when replicating.
build_forensics.baseline_rule: Before trusting delta narratives, verify the Previous/baseline car is stock: cross-check bars + hp + weight + top speed + 0-60 + latG against a car-database stock sheet (kudosprime/calculators.games). A livery icon on the card is NOT evidence of modification. New-column targets are absolute and never depend on this check.
build_forensics.allocation_insight: TWO DIFFERENT 800s: same car, same PI, different part allocation = measurably different cars. The compare pane's live diff QUANTIFIES allocation choices (e.g. race suspension + brakes vs one weight tier + engine trim: -0.29s 0-60 for the weight build). PI-identity is not build-identity — matching the PI number certifies nothing; matching every Car Stat row does.
build_forensics.pane_blind_spots: The compare pane CANNOT see: transmission tier/gear count, driveline, differential tier, tire width, track width (and brakes only indirectly via the braking bar). DOCTRINE REFINEMENT: 'certified replica' = all visible rows matched + PI exact — functionally certified, but blind-spot parts can differ underneath. Driving forensics covers some blind spots: HUD gear count (transmission), 0-60 convergence at equal weight (gearbox character), diff behavior on corner exit.
build_forensics.video_forensics_note: Short gameplay clips are a first-class instrument: frame extraction reads HUD speed/gear/skill-popups per instant. The skill system doubles as telemetry — DRIFT skills during a grip lap = rear slip detected; 'Great Speed' stamps entry speeds; wrecked-scenery skills timestamp off-track moments. 8-10s of video around one corner beats any verbal description.
